children: Japanese rubber futures slipped for a fourth consecutive session on Friday and were set for their biggest weekly loss since late June, pressured by a selloff in Asian equities and soft tyre demand.
The Osaka Exchange (OSE) rubber contract for April delivery
was down 1.2 yen, or 0.28%, at 421.6 yen ($2.64) per kg, as of 0200 GMT
The contract has lost 4.55% so far this week
The rubber contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SHFE) for January delivery
fell 130 yuan, or 0.69%, to 18,595 yuan ($2,789.32) per metric ton
The most active January butadiene rubber contract on the SHFE (SHBRv1) rose 260 yuan, or 1.7%, to 15,525 yuan per metric ton
Recent weak macroeconomic sentiment coupled with sluggish downstream demand has led to a renewed bearish market sentiment, analysts from Gelin Dahua Futures said in a note
tumbled 4.1% and was headed for a 6.8% weekly drop, as Asian shares slid to be on track for their worst week since 2020 after Anthropic's
debut failed to restore investor faith in AI trades, while the dollar extended a rally on safe-haven flows

Capacity utilisation at sampled Chinese semi-steel and all-steel tyre makers was 62.05% and 58.72% in the week ended November 19, down 7.31 and 3.32 percentage points respectively from a year earlier, data from commodity information provider Longzhong Information showed
Raw materials entered a high production phase in top producer Thailand, with rubber tapping operations improving in the northeast region, said analysts from GF Futures in a note
The front-month rubber contract on Singapore Exchange's SICOM platform for February delivery (STFG7) last traded at 238.4 U.S. cents per kg, down 0.7%
